# Part 1: rapid recap 🚀 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## How this part works

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 30px;"}
- I will name a [concept or command]{.alert} from one of the seven lectures
- One of you explains it in [your own words]{.alert} (about 30 seconds)
- The rest of us [push back, add nuance, or correct]{.alert}
- I will keep it moving. Wrong answers are useful; silence is not
- We have about 12 minutes for this section
:::

## Concept 1: the shell

:::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 32px;"}
- Volunteer or victim? 🙋
- In one sentence: [what does the shell do, and why is it useful for data scientists?]{.alert}
- Follow-ups for the room:
  - What is the difference between `bash`, `zsh`, and `fish`?
  - What does it mean for a command to be [piped]{.alert} into another?
  - Give me one [shell command]{.alert} you actually used this week
:::

## Concept 2: file system navigation

:::{style="margin-top: 40px; font-size: 30px;"}
- Pick someone new
- [What do `pwd`, `cd`, `ls`, `mkdir`, `rm` do?]{.alert} (Pair them up: who explains which?)
- Quick room poll: in each case, [is the path absolute or relative?]{.alert}
  - `/Users/danilo/work`
  - `./scripts/run.sh`
  - `~/Documents/datasci350`
  - `../../data/file.csv`
- Connect to: [globbing patterns]{.alert} (`*`, `?`, `[abc]`)
:::

## Concept 3: text-processing tools

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- Three students, one tool each. One sentence per person:
  - [grep]{.alert} — ?
  - [sed]{.alert} — ?
  - [awk]{.alert} — ?
- Then back to the room: name one [real task]{.alert} you would solve with each
- Trick question: how would you [count the number of lines containing the word "error"]{.alert} in a log file?
:::

## Concept 4: Git — local commands

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- This is the single most quiz-worthy concept of the block. 🎯
- Volunteer to explain [the three trees of Git]{.alert} (working directory, staging area, repository)
- Then the room debates:
  - What does `git add .` actually do?
  - What is the difference between `git commit` and `git commit -a`?
  - When would you use `git stash`?
  - What does `HEAD` mean?
- Punchline: a commit is [a snapshot, not a diff]{.alert}
:::

## Concept 5: Git — remote and collaboration

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- Cold call: [what is the difference between `git fetch` and `git pull`?]{.alert}
- Follow-up: [what is a "remote", and why might a repo have more than one?]{.alert}
- Room scenario:
  - You and a partner edit the same file on different branches
  - You push, they push, conflicts arise
  - [Walk me through what happens next]{.alert}
- Connect to: [pull requests, code review, and merge conflicts]{.alert}
:::

## Concept 6: branches and pull requests

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- Pair up with the person next to you. One minute. 🗣️
  - One of you explains [what a branch is]{.alert}
  - The other explains [what a pull request adds on top]{.alert}
- Then I pick two pairs to share
- Rapid-fire room questions:
  - Why is the `main` branch usually [protected]{.alert}?
  - What does it mean to [rebase]{.alert} a branch?
  - When would you choose [merge]{.alert} over [rebase]{.alert}?
:::

## Concept 7: the `.gitignore` and good repository hygiene

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- Last concept of the recap
- [Why do we use `.gitignore`?]{.alert}
- Room:
  - Name three kinds of file you should [never commit]{.alert}
  - What is the danger of committing a `.env` file by mistake?
  - How do you [stop tracking]{.alert} a file you already committed?
:::

# Part 2: a real scenario 🛠️ {background-color="#2d4563"}

## The setup

:::{style="margin-top: 20px; font-size: 26px;"}
:::{.columns}
:::{.column width=60%}
You are joining a small research group, [BrightLab]{.alert}, that does data analysis for a hospital. Your first task: rescue a project that is "almost finished" but has been worked on by three different students over six months.

You clone the repo and find:

- A folder full of `.csv` files, some with the same name and `(1)`, `(2)` suffixes
- Three Jupyter notebooks named `final.ipynb`, `final-v2.ipynb`, `final-v2-DEFINITELY.ipynb`
- A README that mentions "running `process.py`" but no `process.py` exists in the repo
- Branches named `main`, `feature`, `feature-old`, `dani-test`, `delete-me`
- A `.env` file with what looks like a real database password
:::

:::{.column width=40%}
:::{style="text-align: center; margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
🚨

We will work through this together.

I will [not move on]{.alert} until I get answers from at least three different people on each question.
:::
:::
:::
:::

## Question A: triage

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- [What is the first command you run]{.alert} after cloning, and why?
- Hints, if the room is quiet:
  - You want to know [where you are]{.alert} (which branch, which commit)
  - You want to know [what's about to break]{.alert} (uncommitted changes, untracked files)
- Name [at least three useful diagnostic commands]{.alert}
:::

::: {.notes}
Aim for: `git status`, `git log --oneline --graph --all`, `git branch -a`, `ls -la`,
maybe `cat README.md`. The goal is to map the repo before you touch anything.
:::

## Question B: the secret in `.env`

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- The `.env` has a real database password
- Volunteer: [is the secret already exposed?]{.alert}
- Then the room:
  - If `.env` is in the repo and the repo is on GitHub, [what should you assume?]{.alert}
  - Removing it from the working directory and committing — does that fix it?
  - What is the [correct response]{.alert} (treat the password as compromised, rotate it, then clean history)
- This is a classic case of [`.gitignore` should have caught it]{.alert}, but it didn't
:::

## Question C: the Jupyter notebook chaos

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- Three notebooks, all called "final" with version suffixes
- Volunteer: [which one do you trust, and how do you tell?]{.alert}
- Then the room:
  - What does `git log` on a notebook show, vs on a `.py` file?
  - Why are notebooks [hard to diff]{.alert}, and what tools help?
  - If you had to make these reproducible, would you keep them as `.ipynb`, convert to `.py`, or use Quarto?
:::

## Question D: pull request strategy

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- Your team agrees: from now on, every change goes through a pull request
- The room votes by show of hands:
  - [Branch off `main` for every change]{.alert}
  - [Branch off the most recent feature branch]{.alert}
  - [Just push directly when it's a small fix]{.alert}
- Whatever the room votes, I want one defender of each position to [argue for 60 seconds]{.alert}
- Then the room: [what evidence would change your mind?]{.alert}
:::

# Part 3: practice questions 📝 {background-color="#2d4563"}

## How this part works

:::{style="margin-top: 30px; font-size: 28px;"}
- I will show you [three practice questions]{.alert}, one at a time
- They are written in the same style as the real Quiz 01
- Pair up with the person next to you
- You have [two minutes per question]{.alert} to discuss your answer
- Then I will pick a pair to share, and the room critiques
- These are [not the real quiz questions]{.alert}, but the format is identical
:::

## Practice question 1

:::{style="margin-top: 20px; font-size: 26px;"}
You have a folder of 200 CSV files dropped into `~/Downloads/incoming/`. They are all named `report-YYYY-MM-DD.csv`. You want to:

1. Move all of them to `~/work/data/`
2. Print the line count of each file
3. Concatenate them into a single `combined.csv` (preserving the header row only once)

[Your task:]{.alert}

1. Write the [shell commands]{.alert} you would use, in the order you would run them
2. Explain how you would test [whether the move worked correctly]{.alert} before you delete the originals
3. Name one thing that could [go wrong silently]{.alert} (Hint: filename collisions, header rows, encoding)

[Two minutes. Discuss with your partner.]{.alert} ⏱️
:::

## Practice question 2

:::{style="margin-top: 20px; font-size: 26px;"}
A teammate sends you the message: "I committed something secret to the repo by accident. Please help."

You ask them to clarify, and they say:

> I committed `config.py` last week with my AWS access key. I deleted it in a later commit, but it's still in `git log`. The repo is public on GitHub.

[Your task:]{.alert}

1. Is the secret [still exposed]{.alert} despite the deletion? Explain why
2. List the [steps you would take]{.alert} to (a) protect the AWS account and (b) clean the repository
3. What single line in `.gitignore` would have prevented this?

[Two minutes.]{.alert} ⏱️
:::

## Practice question 3

:::{style="margin-top: 20px; font-size: 26px;"}
You are reviewing a pull request from a colleague. The PR has 47 files changed and the description says "small fix to the data pipeline". The diff includes:

- A renamed module
- A new `requirements.txt`
- 12 new tests
- One unrelated commit titled "WIP" 🤔

[Your task:]{.alert}

1. What is your [first concern]{.alert} about this PR?
2. What [questions would you ask the author]{.alert} before approving?
3. If you were the author, [how would you have structured this differently]{.alert} to make review easier?

[Two minutes.]{.alert} ⏱️
:::
